'''Emerald's Dusclops''' (Japanese: '''エメラルドのサマヨール''' ''Emerald's Samayouru'') is a {{OBP|Pokémon|species}} that {{adv|Emerald}} owns in [[Pokémon Adventures]] and his third overall. He is at [[level]] 61 and his [[Characteristic]] is that he is "often lost in thought."

==History==
==={{MangaArc|Emerald}}===
====As a wild Pokémon====
[[File:Emerald Dusclops Battle Pike.png|thumb|150px|left|Dusclops during his time in the Battle Pike]]
Dusclops first appeared in ''[[PS308|As Luck Would Have It, Kirlia]]'', where he was a wild Pokémon in the [[Battle Pike]] that {{adv|Emerald}} had to fight. Dusclops teamed up with a {{p|Kirlia}} to inflict status moves on Emerald's team. Emerald was prepared for this however, and had his Pokémon shake off the statuses and defeated them. After Emerald finished his challenge at the Battle Pike he headed back through the rooms and calmed down the rampaging Pokémon, one of them being Dusclops, who was from [[Mt. Pyre]].

In ''[[PS314|A Sketchy Smattering of Smeargle]]'', it was revealed that Dusclops followed Emerald alongside a {{TP|Emerald|Sudowoodo}} to join Emerald's team. Both of them proceed to help fend off the {{p|Smeargle}} in [[Artisan Cave]] to help Emerald capture {{adv|Jirachi}}. They later defend Emerald from an attack from [[Guile Hideout]], which impressed Emerald enough to let them join him.

====With Emerald====
[[File:Emerald Sceptile Sudowoodo Dusclops.png|thumb|250px|right|Emerald with his Dusclops, Sudowoodo, and Sceptile]]
In ''[[PS317|Sneaky Like Shedinja]]'', Dusclops battled as Emerald's second Pokémon in his battle against [[Greta]]. Emerald had Dusclops use {{m|Psychic}} on {{p|Heracross}}, which gave him good marks on his scores in skill as well as mind and body. Dusclops was easily able to handle Heracross's attack due to {{t|Fighting}} moves having no effect on {{t|Ghost}} types. Due to this Heracross was unable to score enough points, giving Dusclops the win with a score of five to two. For her second Pokémon, Greta sent out {{p|Umbreon}}, which had an advantage over Dusclops. Umbreon attacked with a powerful {{m|Feint Attack}}, knocking Dusclops off balance. Emerald attempted to counterattack with Dusclops's {{m|Will-O-Wisp}}, but Umbreon easily dodged it and confused Dusclops with {{m|Confuse Ray}}, giving Umbreon the win with a score of five to one. Due to Dusclops weakening Umbreon, Sudowoodo was able to finish it off with one {{m|Low Kick}}, giving Emerald the win with a score of two to five.

During the [[Battle Dome]] challenge in ''[[PS320|Verily Vanquishing Vileplume II]]'', Dusclops fought against a {{p|Vileplume}} and easily defeated it with {{m|Fire Punch}}, which Emerald taught to him with Battle Points. Dusclops also fought during his battle against {{adv|Ruby}} and his {{p|Kirlia}}, [[Rara]]. The battle started with Rara using {{m|Hypnosis}} to put Dusclops to {{status|sleep}}, but the {{pkmn|category|Beckon Pokémon}} managed to break himself free from it and respond with a barrage of {{m|Shadow Ball}}s. Surprised to see Rara still standing from the onslaught, Emerald had Dusclops use {{m|Fire Punch}}, which left the Emotion Pokémon with a {{status|burn}}. Although Emerald thought that would help him win, Rara's {{a|Synchronize}} [[Ability]] activated, giving Dusclops a burn as well. This, coupled with Rara using {{m|Imprison}} to keep Dusclops from using Shadow Ball, led to both Pokémon [[fainting]], resulting in a tie. Dusclops was not used during his fight against [[Tucker]] due to Emerald believing he did not need his regular team to win. 
[[File:Feefee battling Amber Gorebyss.png|thumb|160px|Dusclops battling Blaise's Slugma]]
After losing to Tucker, Emerald challenged the [[Battle Palace]] in ''[[PS325|Standing in the Way with Starmie]]''. When Emerald learned that Guile Hideout had captured Jirachi, he left {{TP|Emerald|Sceptile}}, Sudowoodo, and Dusclops to battle [[Spenser]] by themselves while he went to face Guile. In [[PS327|the next chapter]], {{DL|Eon duo (Adventures)|Latios}} returned Emerald's Pokémon, along with the [[Symbol|Spirits Symbol]] they had won in the battle. 

In ''[[PS333|The Final Battle VI]]'', Dusclops joined the rest of Emerald's team in an attempt to attack Guile Hideout. Guile easily fended them off and began attacking them, forcing Emerald to realize he truly cares about Pokémon. Seeing the boy's change of heart, Jirachi grants his wish to free the [[Pokédex holder]]s from petrification. Soon after, he was used to help stop Guile Hideout from escaping.

==={{MangaArc|Omega Ruby & Alpha Sapphire}}===
In ''[[PS604|Goodra Spits]]'', Dusclops battled alongside Sudowoodo to try and hold off [[Zinnia]] from stealing the dimensional shifter. In ''[[PS607|Blastoise Transforms]]'', Dusclops battled [[Blaise]]'s {{p|Slugma}}.

==Personality and characteristics==
In Dusclops's first appearance, he was a rampaging Pokémon that would attack on sight. After {{adv|Emerald}} used his E-Shooter to calm him down he became attached to Emerald and followed him until he joined his team. He cares deeply for his {{pkmn|Trainer}}, and once attempted to suck Emerald into a black hole to have him all to himself.

==Trivia==
* Dusclops is the first {{type|Ghost}} Pokémon to be officially owned by a [[Pokédex holder|main character]] in the [[Pokémon Adventures]] manga.
* Dusclops is the only Pokémon belonging to Emerald that has not reached his final form.
